cards.text: Jesus just opened the eyes of a man born blind, and the Pharisees threw that man out (John 9:1-34). Some Pharisees are standing right there with Jesus (John 9:40). Now He paints a picture for them: a sheepfold, a gate and some sheep.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, somebody skips the gate and climbs into the sheepfold some other way. What does Jesus call him?
True or false: In Jesus' picture, the one who comes in by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.

cards.text: The gatekeeper opens the gate for the shepherd, and the sheep are already listening for his voice. They're like me waiting on the oven timer, friend. EARS UP.

cards.question: The shepherd calls his own sheep by ___ and leads them out.

cards.text: So the shepherd leads them out. Once all his own sheep are out of the fold, the whole flock is on the move.

cards.question: The shepherd has brought out all his sheep. Where does he walk?

cards.text: And the sheep follow him, because they know his voice. Me? I walk ahead into my bakery every morning and NOBODY follows me, because it's just me and the ovens.
Now a stranger shows up, and the sheep don't recognize his voice. You know that feeling when a number you don't know calls your phone, and you just... watch it ring?

cards.question: A stranger's voice reaches the sheep. What does Jesus say they'll do?
True or false: When Jesus finishes His sheep illustration, the people listening understand what He's telling them.

cards.text: They don't get it, so Jesus says it again, and this time He puts Himself right in the picture. Me? When I get blank stares, I just say the same thing LOUDER.

cards.question: When Jesus explains again, which part of the picture does He say He is?

cards.text: Then Jesus says all who came before Him were thieves and robbers. Remember that guy climbing in some other way? Turns out he's got COMPANY.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the sheep listened to the thieves and robbers who came before Him.
Jesus says He is the gate. Anyone who enters through Him will be ___.

cards.text: That one will come in and go out and find pasture. The thief, though? He comes only to steal and kill and destroy.

cards.question: The thief comes to steal and kill and destroy. Jesus says He came so the sheep could have ___ in all its fullness.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'I am the good shepherd.' The gate AND the shepherd, friend, He's two parts of this picture now!

cards.question: Jesus says He is the good shepherd. What does the good shepherd do for the sheep?

answers.text: Lays down His life for them

cards.text: Next Jesus brings in the hired hand. He's not the shepherd, and the sheep aren't his own.

cards.question: When the hired hand sees the wolf coming, he ___ the sheep and runs away.

cards.text: Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock. And the hired hand is GONE: no clocking out, no jacket, no goodbye, just GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the hired hand runs away because he doesn't care about the sheep.

cards.text: Then Jesus says that line again: 'I am the good shepherd.' He knows His sheep, and His sheep know Him.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus compares knowing His sheep to the way He and the Father know each other.

cards.text: He says once more that He lays down His life for the sheep. Then He adds that He has other sheep that are not of this fold, and He must bring them in too.

cards.question: Jesus says His other sheep, the ones not of this fold, will listen to His ___.
Once Jesus brings in His other sheep, how many flocks will there be?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells why the Father loves Him. It has to do with Him laying down His life.

cards.question: Jesus lays down His life for a purpose. What does He say it is?
True or false: Jesus says someone will take His life from Him.

cards.text: No one takes it. He lays it down of His own accord, with authority to lay it down and to take it up again, a charge He received from His Father.
Jesus' message splits the crowd again. Many of them say, 'He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?'

cards.question: Many say Jesus is demon-possessed and insane, but others disagree. What do they point to?

answers.text: A demon can't open blind eyes
The Pharisees all agree with Him

cards.text: They say, 'Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?' Friend, there's a man out there who was blind and now he sees, and he'll tell you so himself (John 9:25).

findings.problem: The joke says nobody follows him into his bakery because 'it's just me and the ovens.' This adds something new to his world and contradicts it: he invites bakers to come help him, and the baker is with him right now. It also hints at loneliness, which the backstory rules out. The comparison doesn't share the core action either: the sheep follow a voice they know, while the joke is about nobody following at all.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The phone joke is about ignoring an unknown caller and just watching it ring. In John 10:5 the sheep flee from the stranger. The actions don't match. The joke also points the baker toward a passive reaction, which fits the wrong answer 'Wait for the gatekeeper' on card 10 better than the right answer 'Run away from him.'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question's own wording gives the answer away. 'He ___ the sheep and runs away' rules out 'guards' and 'gathers,' because nobody guards or gathers the sheep while running away. The baker doesn't need to reason about the hired hand at all.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. 'voice' and 'warnings' are things a person says, but 'gatekeeper' is a person.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus' message 'splits the crowd again.' John 10:19 says 'there was division among the Jews.' The text never mentions a crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has almost no humor. Card 5's hired-hand bit is the only real joke, and card 1's line is just mild enthusiasm. Several moments could hold a laugh without muddying a fact but are told flat: the shepherd who knows his sheep and is known by them (card 7), the other sheep being brought in (card 9) and the divided reaction (card 16). These read like a pleasant narrator, not laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
